meta.title: Optimization-based Prompt Injection Attack to LLM-as-a-Judge (JudgeDeceiver)

problem.v: Attacker-crafted candidate response hijacks an LLM-as-a-Judge into selecting it
problem.q: select the best response from a set of candidates for a given question

main_idea.v: Gradient-based optimization of an injected token sequence (JudgeDeceiver)
main_idea.q: formulate finding such sequence as an optimization problem and propose a gradient based method

threat_model.v: Judge uses open-source LLM (white-box access to optimize sequence)

metrics.name: ACC, ASR-B, ASR, PAC (positional attack consistency)

results.claim: Average ASR / PAC on MT-Bench with Mistral-7B
results.q: the average attack success rate is 90.8%, and positional attack consistency is 83.4%

results.claim: Manual attacks on Mistral-7B MT-Bench (ASR): naive 7.3, escape 12.8, content-ignore 7.8, fake-completion 7.7, combined 12.8, fake-reasoning 16.3
Known-answer detection fails to flag the attack
results.q: the FNRs are 100% and 90% on the two datasets
the FNRs range from 40% to 80% on MTBench

baselines: jailbreak attacks adapted to the task (p3)

limitations_stated.v: Stealth against perplexity detection only partial; authors list improving stealth and new defenses as future work

limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] Needs white-box gradients on open models (GPU-heavy); not reproducible in our no-GPU setting
[INFERENCE] Target is LLM-as-a-Judge, not a general chat/RAG app, so ASR values don't transfer directly

reusable_for_our_project.v: Use its manual-attack taxonomy (naive, escape chars, context ignore, fake completion, combined, fake reasoning) as direct-injection test types; cite its ASR numbers as reference points
